author: Benjamin Yeargin
title: Salmonella now is culprit of BC jail stomach bug cases - NewsBreak
text:
By Benjamin Yeargin ,
8 hours ago
TOWN OF DICKINSON, N.Y. (WIVT/WBGH) – The Broome County Health Department has now determined that salmonella, not norovirus, is the cause for the stomach bug outbreak at the Broome County jail.
News 34 reported earlier today that over 140 incarcerated people were experiencing stomach-bug adjacent symptoms. That number has jumped to over 300. The BC jail is a 536-bed facility.
The original cause was believed to be norovirus, which is a stomach virus that impacts millions of Americans every year. However, testing results from today indicated that salmonella could be the culprit.
Salmonella are bacteria that affect contaminated foods including uncooked meat or unwashed fruits and vegetables.
The BC Health Department have fully inspected the kitchen of the jail where no major violations were reported. The current food supply is being tested to try to determine where prisoners were potentially exposed to salmonella.
“Now that our PCR tests have confirmed Salmonella, we’re confident with our course of treatment for all individuals experiencing these symptoms,” Director of Public Health at the Broome County Health Department Olivia Catalano said.
The BC jail will continue to provide further updates as this story unfolds.
